name: chronicle
description: The build companion itself: a calm macOS app that shows where a multi-phase build stands.

stages.title: Part 1 · Making the old app trustworthy
stages.note: A four-pass audit found 140 problems. These phases fixed the foundation before anything was redrawn.

phases.name: The typed bridge
phases.desc: Give the screen and the engine one clear, checked way to talk to each other, so nothing can call the wrong thing by accident.
items: Name every request the screen can make of the engine, all 28 of them.
Move live terminal output and the window frame onto the same bridge.

phases.name: Trust and safety
phases.desc: Nothing happens to a project without you asking for it, and the app can only ever read inside the folders you opened.
items: Ask before a background session ever starts, and make Cancel actually stop it.
Fence every file read to the projects you opened, refusing shortcuts that point outside.
Clean up every background process when a window closes.

paste.when: a fresh session at the project root

phases.name: One-click helpers
phases.desc: Replace copy-this-command chips with buttons that just do the thing, and make the file reader notice when a file changed underneath it.
items: Turn save, publish and bring down into real buttons.
Tell you honestly when what you are reading is no longer what is on disk.

paste.when: continuing the hardening pass

phases.name: Honest rules
phases.desc: The roadmap engine only ever claims what it can prove, and a locked-down test proves it keeps doing so.
items: A rule the app cannot check is shown as unknown, never quietly counted as done.
A repeatable test pins the engine's answers so a future change cannot drift them.
Chronicle starts using its own roadmap file on itself.

paste.when: continuing the hardening pass

phases.name: The task board engine
phases.desc: Write bugs and ideas down as cards, attach screenshots, and freeze a batch of them into a round the agent can work through.
items: Cards, columns and attachments, stored inside the project so they travel with it.
A frozen round turns into a plan file, a prompt file, and a phase on the roadmap.

paste.when: continuing the hardening pass

phases.name: Every screen gets drawn
phases.desc: The whole app is redesigned from scratch on the Weave design system. Six decks, thirty frames, every state drawn before any of it is built.
items: Send the full design brief out as one batch.
Comps come back and are read against the brief frame by frame.
The accepted decks become a written contract the build has to match.

paste.when: one paste, the whole batch at once

stages.title: Part 3 · Building version 2
stages.note: One slice at a time, each checked against its deck before the next one starts.

phases.name: The opening screen and its dialogs
phases.desc: The screen you land on: your recent projects, the switcher, and every confirm and warning that can appear over it.

paste.when: the contract each slice is built against

phases.name: The window frame and sidebar
phases.desc: Project tabs along the top, the three-surface sidebar down the left, and the honest line that tells you when something is degraded.

phases.name: The roadmap
phases.desc: The main view: where the build stands right now, what needs you, the always-on documents, and the phase timeline.

phases.name: Phase detail
phases.desc: One phase opened up: its steps, the exact files to paste and where they go, and the saves that belong to it.

phases.name: Files and history
phases.desc: The file tree, a reader that knows when a file changed on disk, and your project history in plain words instead of git jargon.

phases.name: Terminals
phases.desc: Real shells inside the app, surviving pane and project switches, with tab labels that tell the truth about what is running.

phases.name: The task board
phases.desc: The kanban board built to its deck: cards, columns, attachments, and the ready-to-execute flow that freezes a round.

phases.name: The rebuild replaces the old app
phases.desc: Version 2 becomes the real app and ships as 0.2.0.

phases.name: The feature batch
phases.desc: Seven features land together on top of the rebuild and ship as 0.2.0.

phases.name: Twelve small releases
phases.desc: 0.2.1 through 0.2.12: the agent-resolution fix, the self-installing skill, and seven rounds of bug fixes worked off the task board.
items: Each round of bugs was frozen on the board, written up as a plan and a prompt, and worked through.
139 of the 140 audit findings are closed.

stages.title: Part 5 · The agent arrives (0.3)
stages.note: Chronicle stops watching Claude Code from the outside and starts driving it.

phases.name: The agent designs
phases.desc: Deck 7 is drawn and accepted: the chat thread, the tool cards, the permission cards, and every state the pane can be in.

paste.when: one paste, before any pane is built

phases.name: The agent bridge
phases.desc: The engine can start a real Claude Code session, send it a message, stream back what it says, and answer its permission questions.
items: Everything the agent writes is fenced to the folders you opened.
Every change is recorded before it lands, so it can always be undone.
A cancelled turn can never leave a question hanging.

paste.when: a fresh session at the project root

phases.name: The three-part window
phases.desc: The right side stacks the agent above the terminal. Content, agent and terminal each show or hide on their own, and the last one open always stays open.

paste.when: continuing the agent update

phases.name: The agent pane
phases.desc: The pane itself, built to Deck 7: the thread, a card for every kind of thing the agent does, and the box you type into.

paste.when: continuing the agent update

phases.name: Review and undo
phases.desc: Every file the agent touched is reviewable, keepable and undoable, one at a time or all at once. A snapshot before each message lets you rewind to any point in the conversation.
items: Undo still works after you quit and reopen the app.
Files the agent created are deleted again when you rewind past them.

paste.when: continuing the agent update

phases.name: Wired into Chronicle
phases.desc: Starting a phase and running a round of fixes both land in the agent pane, and past conversations can be reopened or picked back up.
items: A phase prompt arrives unsent, so you can read it before it goes.
A round is only called done when the board says so, never because the agent claimed it.

paste.when: continuing the agent update

phases.name: Five refinements
phases.desc: Plain-English publish and bring-down results, clickable file paths in the terminal, honest terminal tab labels, a better save-message prompt, and a real progress bar for app updates.

paste.when: continuing the agent update

phases.name: Ship 0.3.0
phases.desc: The full sweep, then a signed and notarized release with an over-the-air update for everyone already running Chronicle.

phases.name: 0.3.1 and 0.3.2
phases.desc: The agent could not find Node when Chronicle was launched from the Finder, and it would not start on its own when Claude was already installed. Both fixed and released.

stages.title: Part 7 · Getting set up without a terminal (0.4)
stages.note: The point where Chronicle stops assuming you already have a developer machine.

phases.name: The setup and help designs
phases.desc: Deck 8 is drawn and accepted: the setup checklist in every state, the repair flows, the sign-in hand-offs, and the help screen.

paste.when: one paste, before any screen is built

phases.name: The doctor
phases.desc: The part that works out what your machine is missing and installs it for you, with no password prompts and nothing touched outside your own home folder.
items: Six checks: Claude, signing in to Claude, Node, terminal access, GitHub, and the plugin pack.
Downloads are checked against the vendor's own checksum before anything is unpacked.
The terminal-access repair writes one fenced block and never overwrites something you wrote by hand.

paste.when: a fresh session at the project root

phases.name: The setup screen
phases.desc: The checklist you actually see, with a live percentage while things install, an honest message when one fails, and a Set everything up for me button.
items: It appears over the opening screen the first time something is missing, and stays reachable afterwards as a health check.
Signing in opens a real Terminal window, and the row advances by itself once you are through.

paste.when: continuing the setup update

phases.name: The help screen
phases.desc: Seven how-do-I recipes that can take you to the right screen, a plain glossary, the real keyboard shortcuts, and one search across all of it.

paste.when: continuing the setup update

phases.name: Ship 0.4.0
phases.desc: Setup, help, and the agent pane reshaped into a real chat, released together. Two invisible-button bugs and a false sign-in warning were caught and fixed on the way.

stages.title: Part 8 · A composer that feels like a chat box (0.5)
stages.note: Five small changes to the box you type into.

phases.name: Somewhere for attachments to live
phases.desc: A file you attach is copied into the project so the agent can read it from disk, never clobbering a file that is already there.

paste.when: a fresh session at the project root

phases.name: A warning before Full auto
phases.desc: Turning the agent fully loose asks you once per session first, so it can never happen by a stray click.

paste.when: continuing the composer update

done_when.commit_subject: (?i)warn once per session before full auto

phases.name: Enter sends, and the box grows
phases.desc: Enter sends the message, Shift and Enter adds a line, and the box grows as you type instead of scrolling inside itself.

paste.when: continuing the composer update

phases.name: Attach files
phases.desc: Add a file by picking it, dragging it in from the Finder, or pasting a screenshot straight from the clipboard.

paste.when: continuing the composer update

phases.name: Drag a file into a terminal
phases.desc: Hold Shift and drag an attachment onto a terminal to type its path there. It never presses Enter for you.

paste.when: the last task of the composer update

done_when.commit_subject: (?i)shift-drag an attachment path into a terminal

stages.title: Part 9 · Four things the chat was missing (0.5)

phases.name: Choose how hard it thinks
phases.desc: An effort picker next to the model picker, built from whatever the agent itself says it offers. If it offers nothing, nothing is shown.

paste.when: a fresh session at the project root

phases.name: Line messages up mid-turn
phases.desc: Type while the agent is still working and your messages queue up, then send themselves in order when the turn ends.

paste.when: continuing the chat update

phases.name: See the edit, side by side
phases.desc: Open any edit card in the conversation into a before-and-after view without leaving the chat.

paste.when: continuing the chat update

done_when.commit_subject: (?i)expand edit tool cards to a side-by-side diff

phases.name: The agent's own plan, live
phases.desc: When the agent writes itself a to-do list, that list appears in the chat and ticks itself off as it goes.

paste.when: the last task of the chat update

phases.name: Ship 0.5.0
phases.desc: The composer and chat updates released together, with Stop no longer throwing away your queued messages.

phases.name: Polish and a full icon sweep
phases.desc: The composer tidied up and every icon in the app redrawn as a proper vector. Released as 0.5.1.

stages.title: Part 11 · The composer's menus
stages.note: Shipped in 0.6.0. There is no written plan for this one in the repo, so the roadmap follows the saves instead.

phases.name: The slash menu
phases.desc: Typing a slash opens a menu of everything you can run. The agent's own commands and skills sit under their plugin's name, and Chronicle's own commands sit under their own heading so you can see which ones never reach the agent.
items: The agent's commands arrive over the wire, so a project skill needs no special handling.
Chronicle's own commands run against the session in front of you: undo, keep, rewind.
Arrow keys move and Enter picks, and Enter never sends the message while the menu is open.

paste.label: the plan for the composer menus
paste.when: Never written down. It was built straight from the saves.

phases.name: The @ menu for files
phases.desc: Typing an at-sign opens the same menu against your project's files, so you can point the agent at something without typing out a path.
items: The same menu, the same keys, pointed at your files instead of your commands.
Picking a file drops its path in where you were typing.

paste.label: the plan for the composer menus
paste.when: Never written down. It was built straight from the saves.

phases.name: Drag files in from the Finder
phases.desc: Drop a file from the Finder onto a terminal to type its path there, or onto the chat box to attach it. Released as 0.7.0.

stages.title: Part 13 · A quieter app, a browser, notes and editing (0.8)
stages.note: Four written plans, built one after another and released together as 0.8.0, with a steadier window following in 0.8.1.

phases.name: An idle window that costs nothing
phases.desc: When nobody is looking at Chronicle it stops waking itself up, stops starting background programs, and stops redrawing. On battery it slows down further.
items: Every timer runs through one scheduler that knows whether the window is visible, focused, or on battery.
The engine announces when a session changes instead of the screen asking every few seconds.
The agent pane starts hidden, so the agent only starts when you open it.
Measured: an idle window went from 3 to 1 unit of work a second when focused, and from 5 to 0 when hidden.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

phases.name: The Web pane
phases.desc: A fourth pane that browses the web and shows HTML pages from your project inside Chronicle, with ads and trackers blocked.
items: Each tab is a real browser view, and it costs nothing while you are not looking at it.
The same block lists uBlock uses, built into the app.
Command-clicking a Claude artifact link or an HTML file in a terminal opens it here.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

phases.name: Notes replace the task board
phases.desc: The task board becomes a folder of plain notes inside the project: a rich editor, links between notes, tags and search. A note with a status is a task, and a round takes the queued ones.
items: Your existing board is moved into notes the first time the project opens, all or nothing.
Rounds of fixes now run from notes, and a note is locked while a round is working on it.
The notes are ordinary markdown files, so they read fine outside Chronicle too.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

phases.name: Editing files, and an honest history
phases.desc: The Repo pane becomes a place you can work: edit a file and save it yourself, make, rename and bin files, and see four plain facts about your project's history instead of a guess.
items: Nothing saves until you press Command S, and a bar warns you when the agent changed the file underneath you.
Deleted files go to the Trash, never straight to gone.
Checking for new saves online only happens when you press Check now.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

phases.name: A steadier window, and web tabs in folders
phases.desc: The window no longer tears or flashes grey while you resize it, web tabs move into a sidebar with folders, and the agent's permission mode becomes a dropdown. Released as 0.8.1.

stages.title: Part 14 · A roadmap that stays true, and agents that can read it (0.9)

phases.name: A roadmap that never goes backwards
phases.desc: A finished phase stays finished, every done phase says what proved it, and the roadmap notices when it has fallen behind the project and offers to bring itself up to date.
items: A save can carry a one-line marker that proves a phase is done, whatever the other rules say.
Chronicle remembers every phase it has ever seen finished, so a rule that stops matching can't undo it.
New plans and newer releases the roadmap never saw show up under what needs you, with one button to catch up.
Phase detail shows the proof, and lets you mark a phase done or not done by hand.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

phases.name: Notes and roadmap state, for any agent
phases.desc: An agent, or you at a terminal, can list, read, write and update a project's notes and ask where the roadmap stands, without the app even running.
items: The same answers the app shows, reached two ways: as a tool the agent can call, or as a command you type.
Reading the state never changes anything.
A second copy of the project on another branch shares the main copy's notes.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

phases.name: Ship 0.9.0
phases.desc: Built, signed and tagged, with the roadmap work, a single look for every popup and menu, and the first half of agent access. It was never put out for download, because 0.10.0 followed the same day.

stages.title: Part 15 · Agents that act, in plain view (0.10)

phases.name: Rounds you can watch
phases.desc: A round of fixes never runs out of sight again. Planning it is a turn in the agent pane, and running it happens in the pane or in a terminal tab you can watch.
items: The hidden background sessions, their log panel and the progress window are gone.
A round started while the agent is busy waits its turn in the queue, and is asked again before it sends.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

done_when.commit_subject: (?i)docs\(rounds\): what changed when rounds became visible

phases.name: Agents can act, when you let them
phases.desc: An agent can plan or start a round, open a project, and read a terminal, and every one of those happens on screen using the same code as the buttons.
items: Nothing is reachable until you switch on Let agents reach Chronicle for that project in Setup, and one click takes it back.
The app only answers its own private connection, and only for projects you have open.
When Chronicle isn't open, the agent is told so plainly instead of failing silently.

paste.when: A fresh session at the project root

done_when.commit_subject: (?i)docs\(agent\): actions, the bridge, and the opt-in row

phases.name: Ship 0.10.0
phases.desc: Rounds you can watch and agent actions, released together. This is the version that went out for download.

stages.title: Part 16 · One Chronicle, a thread you can read, notes that name themselves (0.11)
stages.note: Two rounds of fixes from Notes, released together. The rounds themselves also appear under Fixes & ideas.

phases.name: Ship 0.11.0
phases.desc: Rounds 8 and 9, plus a few fixes, released together.
items: Asking the app for help from the command line no longer opens another Chronicle window, and a second launch hands off to the one already running.
The work a helper agent does sits in a tree under the card that started it, and the agent's thinking is kept and folded away.
Your usage limits and this session's cost show live in the title bar.
Notes name themselves from their first line until you rename them by hand, and can be dragged between folders.
An arrow key at the end of a field no longer types a square, and a resumed session opens on its conversation.

phases.name: Ship 0.11.1
phases.desc: Websites in the Web pane stop asking you to update your browser, and the agent's conversation moves smoothly as new rows arrive.

stages.title: Part 17 · What comes next
stages.note: Written down and agreed. Steps that tick themselves has shipped; the rest has not started.

phases.name: One pane, any agent
phases.desc: The pane is written around Claude Code today. This makes it read whatever agent is on the other end, so Codex and the rest can sit in the same chat.

phases.name: Steps that tick themselves
phases.desc: Right now a phase's steps stay grey until the whole phase turns green. This lets a single step carry its own proof, so a phase can honestly read three of five.
items: A step may stay a plain sentence, or gain a rule of its own.
The app that can read the new shape has to reach everyone before anything starts writing it.
A finished phase always shows all its steps finished, whatever the step rules say.

phases.name: The idea shelf
phases.desc: Deliberately set aside when the agent landed. Each one was deferred, not rejected.
items: Sandboxing the machine while the agent is running fully loose.
Saving a conversation out, and bringing one back in.
Branch and stash pickers, and who-changed-this-line.
Running Codex through the same bridge, once its adapter is ready.
